cost_model.primary_definition: analysis-grade: C_SBS / C_VBS / selected-solver costs from the benchmark's warm-up+repetitions medians; SelectionOverhead measured on the real adaptive path; C_Adaptive = SelectionOverhead + C_selected_solver
cost_model.secondary_definition: measured end-to-end: every solver call single-shot inside the adaptive loop, which is the only modality in which C_Adaptive - C_SBS is a paired difference
cost_model.selection_charge: measured single-row latency; library and compiled-rule modes reported separately

sbs.assertion: reference graphs disjoint from validation and test graphs

adaptive.measurement: end-to-end wall clock of the adaptive path only; SBS/VBS paired in an adjacent loop

adaptive_minus_sbs_seconds.caveat: 8 purposively designed test graphs; intervals bound this sample, not a population of graphs

adaptive_ratio_sbs.caveat: 8 purposively designed test graphs; intervals bound this sample, not a population of graphs

oracle_gap_seconds.caveat: 8 purposively designed test graphs; intervals bound this sample, not a population of graphs

oracle_gap_noise_bound.meaning: benchmark repeated-median gap vs paired single-shot gap

compiled_variant.verdict: nominal gains are far below the pass-to-pass dispersion; not a crossover

Q1_adaptive_beats_sbs_anywhere.evidence: Primary configuration: 0 of 40 graph x Q cells have adaptive below SBS; the smallest loss is +0.378 ms (single graph, Q=500). With compiled-rule inference (a deployment variant, not the primary configuration) 4 of 40 cells are nominally below SBS, by at most 2.419 ms = 0.23% of the Q=500 SBS cost, i.e. far inside the 9% pass-to-pass dispersion of the same quantity; these are not reported as a crossover.

Q2_why_not.solver_side: The selector's expected solver cost equals the SBS policy's: solver-only capture = -0.1633 of the oracle gap at Q=500 (chosen-solver total 1084.210 ms vs SBS 1064.200 ms).
Q2_why_not.overhead_side: Required capture at Q=500 is 3.853 of the oracle gap with library per-query inference and 0.290 with compiled rules; the oracle gap is only 11.51% of the SBS cost.

Q3_vbs_headroom.evidence: Oracle gap over 8 test graphs and 4,000 queries at Q=500: 122.523 ms = 11.51% of the SBS policy cost. VBS wins overall: Bidirectional Dijkstra takes most instances.

Q4_capture.evidence: CaptureRate at Q=500 = -4.0160; required = 3.8527. Solver-only (overhead-free) capture = -0.1633.

Q5_capture_vs_Q.answer: Capture is roughly Q-independent and never positive at aggregate level.

Q6_required_capture_vs_Q.answer: Required capture falls with Q because the graph-level feature cost is paid once and the per-query costs are roughly constant while the cumulative oracle gap grows.

Q7_tier_expansion.answer: No. Richer features cost more than they return.
Q7_tier_expansion.evidence: Analysis-grade required capture at Q=500: tier 0 = 2.828 (library) / 0.114 (compiled); exact accuracy is statistically indistinguishable across tiers.

Q8_generalizes_to_unseen_configurations.evidence: Primary tier 1: leave-one-cell-out median exact accuracy 80.80% vs majority 77.95% (median lift +0.00pp over 24 folds); the tree predicts a constant solver in 9 of those folds.

Q9_generalizes_across_families.evidence: Primary tier 1: leave-one-family-out median exact accuracy 79.09% vs majority 83.45% (median lift +0.00pp over 3 folds); the tree predicts a constant solver in 1 of those folds.

Q1b_compiled_variant_nominal_wins.answer: Nominally, with compiled-rule inference, a small number of graph x Q cells sit a fraction of a percent below SBS; the margin is one to two orders of magnitude smaller than the pass-to-pass dispersion of the same quantity, so it is not a reproducible crossover.
Q1b_compiled_variant_nominal_wins.evidence: 4 of 40 cells below SBS, largest -2.419 ms; pass-to-pass dispersion of the same aggregate wall clock 9.4%.

Q10_bottleneck.answer: Selector efficacy is the binding constraint whenever inference is cheap (compiled rules); per-query selection overhead is the binding constraint when inference goes through a general-purpose model library. Solver diversity is not the constraint.
Q10_bottleneck.evidence: compiled: required 0.290 < 1.0, so even a perfect selector would pay, but achievable capture is -0.1633. library: required 3.853 > 1.0, so no selector could pay.
